Maya: Pushed a new candidate to staging: `pegasus-embed-lite-int4` (quant per-channel). Did a quick run on webdocs-shorttail and seeing weird behaviour on very short queries (<=8 tokens).
Liam: can you paste the run command + top-line metrics?
Maya: ran the eval script: ```./eval_embeddings.py --model pegasus-embed-lite-int4 --dataset webdocs-shorttail --k 1,5,10 --seed 42 --batch-size 256```
Maya: top-line: recall@1 dropped from 0.72 -> 0.58, recall@10 from 0.91 -> 0.89. avg cosine sim shifted by -0.03 on short queries. full logs attached to staging job 8792.
Sasha: hmm, recall@1 drop for short queries only? what about long queries?
Maya: long queries (>=50 tokens) practically unchanged. This looks like a short-tail failure mode.
Liam: any clue from the embedding norms / scale? can you dump norms distribution?
Maya: pasted a quick ASCII histogram: ``norm<0.5: 2.1% | 0.5-1.0: 18.9% | 1.0-1.5: 55.0% | >1.5: 24.0%``. Compared to baseline (pegasus-embed-fp16): slightly tighter mass -> possible compression artifact.
Ramon: did you try recalibrating with L2 normalisation at inference time? (we usually normalize for cosine).
Maya: yes, both normalized and raw scores tested. Normalization helped overall but recall@1 still low for short queries vs baseline normalized.
Sasha: could be embedding collapse on short contexts — maybe quantization of the first attention layers. Any per-layer quant diffs?
Maya: we enabled per-channel int4 on the projection matrices, CPU fallback for some ops. I ran a cheap ablation switching per-channel -> per-tensor and saw recall@1 improve ~+0.03 but latency up ~7%.
Liam: interesting. Also run a cluster stability check? if centroids move that's a red flag for retrieval systems.
Maya: ran a single-pass kmeans on the dev index (k=1000) and computed chi2 between cluster assignments (baseline vs candidate). Chi2 ~ 12.6, p-value < 0.001 (so assignments aren't identical). silhouette dropped from 0.21 -> 0.16 for short queries subset.
Sasha: can you add a small sample where candidate mismatches baseline recall@1? maybe inspect top-3 neighbors.
Maya: sample entry:
```
query: "install gcloud sdk"
baseline top1: doc_532 (sim=0.84)
candidate top1: doc_1102 (sim=0.60)
baseline top3: [532, 781, 101]
candidate top3: [1102, 532, 781]
```
Maya: candidate still finds the right doc but ranks it lower. seems like subtle score compression.
Ramon: could be quantization zeroing small but important components. Try tiny asymmetric calibration (offset) for int4, and a test with per-channel-clip values.
Liam: also try microbatch 64 vs 256 — batching interacts with KV cache priming and may change prefix state for short queries.
Maya: did batchsize 64/256/1024: no meaningful delta for recall (within noise).
Sasha: what about training-time vs inference tokenization differences? short queries more sensitive.
Maya: tokenizer same, but candidate model uses fused embedding table op, baseline uses old path. I suspect fused op quant rounding.
Liam: can you run a targeted eval: 1) per-channel->per-tensor ablation, 2) asymmetric calibration, 3) revert fused-embed -> old path, and 4) 1000-sample short-query recall scatter to compute ID flip rate.
Maya: on it. kicking off 4 jobs now, names: peg-ablate-pt, peg-asym-cal, peg-embed-fallback, peg-shortflip-1k. devops-bot: created staging jobs 8810-8813.
Devops-bot: staging job 8810 queued; 8811 queued; 8812 queued; 8813 queued.
Ramon: if embed fallback fixes it, we can keep quant config but route embed table to fp16 fused implementation as a fast mitigant.
Sasha: also add a cheap eval: recall@1 stratified by token-length bins [1-5,6-10,11-20,21+]. that'll make the short-tail regression obvious in the dashboard.
Maya: added stratified eval to the job config.
Liam: thanks. once we have the ablation outputs, let's produce a one-slide summary with recommended config (perf vs quality tradeoffs).
Maya: will do. leaving initial logs in /mnt/staging/pegasus-shorttail/8792 and will post results when jobs finish. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Sasha: thanks — ping us when the top cases are logged so we can check for semantic pattern (e.g., imperative search queries vs named entities).
Maya: will share top-50 mismatch pairs.
Ramon: FYI, if this becomes a recurring short-tail pattern across other models, might be worth adding a short-query eval harness to our CI (fast, 1k queries).
Liam: agreed. low-cost guardrails are helpful.
Maya: noted. will open a follow-up PR adding the harness if ablations point at a quant config fix.
Maya: quick status update (later): peg-embed-fallback (8812) improved recall@1 on short queries from 0.58 -> 0.69, still trailing baseline 0.72. per-tensor quant (8810) got to 0.66. asym-cal (8811) 0.63. shortflip-1k (8813) ID-flip rate 4.8% vs baseline 1.3%.
Sasha: fallback looks promising. can we ship with embed fallback in Dedicated, keep default per-channel for Hosted where latency matters?
Ramon: we'll quantify p99 latency delta; embed fallback increased mean latency by 4% on staging GPUs.
Liam: create a recommendation: default per-channel int4, but route small short-query traffic to an embed-fallback variant for strict recall SLO customers. Draft that in the release note.
Maya: drafting release note + PR for staged rollout (canary 5% then 20%). will include stratified histograms and a small remediation playbook.
Devops-bot: job 8812 (peg-embed-fallback) completed successfully.
Maya: attaching CSV with top-50 mismatch pairs and a short writeup to the thread.
